text: You already learned to read an encoded query off a list's breadcrumb earlier in this path. Today that same string becomes real, executable input to GlideRecord, plus a handful of other addQuery variants you'll use constantly once basic equals-only filtering isn't enough.

addEncodedQuery takes that exact breadcrumb syntax — active equals true, caret, priority equals one — and runs it as the filter. The caret means AND between conditions, caret-OR means OR, exactly what you already know. This one string is equivalent to two separate addQuery calls, and it's especially useful when a query is built dynamically from a string, like one copied from a list view's URL or passed into a Script Include.

addQuery with two arguments always means equals. For any other comparison, pass the operator explicitly as a third argument — priority less-than-or-equal-to 2 gets you priority 1 or 2, and sys_created_on greater-than a date gets you anything newer. Common operators include equals, not equals, greater than, less than, IN, STARTSWITH, and CONTAINS.

addNullQuery filters for a field being empty — unassigned incidents, for example. addNotNullQuery is the opposite, filtering for the field having a value. And addOrCondition chains an OR onto the addQuery call it's attached to — priority 1 addOrCondition priority 2 means priority 1 OR priority 2, as one group, which still combines with AND against everything else on the GlideRecord.

orderBy sorts ascending, orderByDesc sorts descending. Here's the trap: in ServiceNow, priority 1 is the most urgent, the lowest number — so orderBy on priority lists the most urgent incidents first, not last. Always double-check which direction you actually want before assuming descending means most urgent first.

Encoded queries, operators, null checks, OR conditions, and sorting — that's the full addQuery toolkit, and it covers nearly every filter you'll ever need to express. Next lesson, we look at the performance pitfalls that show up once your queries get used inside loops and scheduled jobs at scale.
